### Chapter 18: Parametric Portfolio Policies {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: sol-18-setup
#| include: false
source("R/_common.R")
library(tidypm)
# The chapter's panels and functions, rebuilt so that this fragment runs on its own.
R  <- as_xts_pm(sim_class_returns_monthly, date, class, return)
eq <- sim_assets$asset_id[sim_assets$asset_class == "equity"]
Ra <- as_xts_pm(dplyr::filter(sim_asset_returns_monthly, asset %in% eq), date, asset, return)
dates <- zoo::index(R); Tn <- nrow(R); gamma <- 5
held <- 14:Tn; known <- held - 1L
lag_rows <- function(M, k) rbind(matrix(NA_real_, k, ncol(M)), M[seq_len(nrow(M) - k), , drop = FALSE])
zscore   <- function(M) (M - rowMeans(M)) / apply(M, 1, stats::sd)
mom_12_1 <- function(Rm) { P <- apply(1 + Rm, 2, cumprod); lag_rows(P, 1) / lag_rows(P, 12) - 1 }
cap <- sim_marketcap_weekly |> dplyr::filter(asset %in% eq) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = asset, values_from = market_cap) |> dplyr::arrange(date)
ME <- as.matrix(cap[findInterval(dates, cap$date), colnames(Ra)])
region <- sim_assets$region[match(colnames(Ra), sim_assets$asset_id)]
within_region <- function(M) { for (g in unique(region)) M[, region == g] <- zscore(M[, region == g]); M }
panel <- function(chars, Rm) {
  X <- array(unlist(lapply(chars, function(M) M[known, ])), c(length(held), ncol(Rm), length(chars)),
             dimnames = list(as.character(dates[held]), colnames(Rm), names(chars)))
  Rn <- Rm[held, ]; rownames(Rn) <- dimnames(X)[[1]]
  stopifnot(!anyNA(X), max(abs(apply(X, c(1, 3), sum))) < 1e-10)
  list(X = X, Rn = Rn)
}
Rm_eq <- zoo::coredata(Ra); mom_eq <- mom_12_1(Rm_eq)
p_eq <- panel(list(size = within_region(log(ME)), momentum = within_region(mom_eq)), Rm_eq)
X_eq <- p_eq$X; Rn_eq <- p_eq$Rn
wbar_eq <- (ME / rowSums(ME))[known, ]; dimnames(wbar_eq) <- dimnames(Rn_eq)
ppp_weights <- function(theta, X, wbar, long_only = FALSE) {
  tilt <- 0
  for (k in seq_along(theta)) tilt <- tilt + theta[k] * X[, , k]
  w <- wbar + tilt / ncol(wbar)
  if (long_only) { w <- pmax(w, 0); w <- w / rowSums(w) }
  w
}
crra <- function(r, gamma) (1 + r)^(1 - gamma) / (1 - gamma)
path_returns <- function(W, Rn, cost) {
  gross <- rowSums(W * Rn); hold <- W * (1 + Rn) / (1 + gross)
  trade <- abs(W - rbind(0, hold[-nrow(W), , drop = FALSE]))
  cbind(gross = gross, net = gross - as.numeric(trade %*% cost), turnover = rowSums(trade) / 2)
}
ppp_utility <- function(theta, X, wbar, Rn, cost = NULL, gamma = 5, long_only = FALSE) {
  W <- ppp_weights(theta, X, wbar, long_only)
  r <- if (is.null(cost)) rowSums(W * Rn) else path_returns(W, Rn, cost)[, "net"]
  mean(crra(r, gamma))
}
ppp_estimate <- function(X, wbar, Rn, cost = NULL, gamma = 5, start = rep(0, dim(X)[3])) {
  f <- function(th) -ppp_utility(th, X, wbar, Rn, cost, gamma)
  setNames(stats::optim(start, f, method = "BFGS", control = list(reltol = 1e-12))$par, dimnames(X)[[3]])
}
theta_eq <- ppp_estimate(X_eq, wbar_eq, Rn_eq)
```

#### Exercise 1

Standardizing across all names makes size partly a region characteristic,
because the US names are the largest. The coefficients move and, more to the
point, the policy now takes a regional bet that the region-neutral version
did not: its average weight in US names drifts away from the benchmark's.

```{r}
#| label: sol-18-ex1
p_gl <- panel(list(size = zscore(log(ME)), momentum = zscore(mom_eq)), Rm_eq)
theta_gl <- ppp_estimate(p_gl$X, wbar_eq, p_gl$Rn)
us <- region == "US"
us_share <- function(W) mean(rowSums(W[, us]))
round(rbind(within_region = c(theta_eq, us_share = us_share(ppp_weights(theta_eq, X_eq, wbar_eq))),
            global        = c(theta_gl, us_share = us_share(ppp_weights(theta_gl, p_gl$X, wbar_eq))),
            benchmark     = c(NA, NA, us_share = us_share(wbar_eq))), 3)
```

The within-region policy holds exactly the benchmark's US share by
construction; the global one does not, and the difference is the region bet
of @sec-05-factor-models-implementation entering through the back door.

#### Exercise 2

```{r}
#| label: sol-18-ex2
by_gamma <- t(vapply(c(2, 5, 10), function(g) {
  th <- ppp_estimate(X_eq, wbar_eq, Rn_eq, gamma = g)
  W  <- ppp_weights(th, X_eq, wbar_eq)
  c(gamma = g, th, theta_x_gamma = unname(th[["size"]] * g), short = mean(rowSums(pmin(W, 0))))
}, numeric(5)))
round(by_gamma, 2)
```

The product of the size coefficient and $\gamma$ is roughly constant, so the
tilt scales close to $1/\gamma$, as the invested fraction of
@eq-03-separation does; it is not exact because power utility is not
quadratic. The short side shrinks faster than $1/\gamma$, because the
leverage of the policy falls with the size of every tilt.

#### Exercise 3

```{r}
#| label: sol-18-ex3
cost_at <- function(bp) setNames(rep(bp / 1e4, ncol(Ra)), colnames(Ra))
th_10 <- ppp_estimate(X_eq, wbar_eq, Rn_eq, cost_at(10), start = theta_eq)
th_50 <- ppp_estimate(X_eq, wbar_eq, Rn_eq, cost_at(50), start = theta_eq)
char_turnover <- apply(X_eq, 3, function(M) mean(abs(diff(M))))   # mean monthly change of a standardized characteristic
round(rbind(no_cost = theta_eq, bp_10 = th_10, bp_50 = th_50, char_turnover = char_turnover), 3)
```

Momentum is the characteristic that changes fastest from month to month, so
its tilt is the expensive one to hold and its coefficient shrinks most as the
cost rate rises, exactly as @eq-18-cost implies.

#### Exercise 4

```{r}
#| label: sol-18-ex4
grp <- sub(".*_", "", colnames(R))
cv <- sim_curve_weekly |> dplyr::filter(series %in% c("US_Slope", "US_IG_Spread")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = series, values_from = value) |> dplyr::arrange(date)
j_last <- findInterval(dates, cv$date)
expanding_z <- function(x, first = 12L, clip = 2) {
  z <- vapply(seq_along(x), function(t) if (t < first) NA_real_ else (x[t] - mean(x[1:t])) / stats::sd(x[1:t]), numeric(1))
  pmax(pmin(z, clip), -clip)
}
loading <- function(g) { x <- as.numeric(grp == g); (x - mean(x)) / stats::sd(x) }
Rm_cl <- zoo::coredata(R)
p_cl <- panel(list(momentum = zscore(mom_12_1(Rm_cl)),
                   term = outer(expanding_z(-cv$US_Slope[j_last]), loading("government")),
                   credit = outer(expanding_z(cv$US_IG_Spread[j_last]), loading("credit"))), Rm_cl)
ins <- held <= 120L
X_i <- p_cl$X[ins, , ]; R_i <- p_cl$Rn[ins, ]; w_i <- R_i; w_i[] <- 1 / ncol(R)
f_trunc <- function(th) -ppp_utility(th, X_i, w_i, R_i, long_only = TRUE)
fits <- lapply(list(c(0.3, 0.2, 0.2), c(3, 2, 2)), function(s)
  stats::optim(s, f_trunc, method = "Nelder-Mead", control = list(maxit = 400)))
round(rbind(start_small = c(fits[[1]]$par, utility = -fits[[1]]$value, scale = sum(abs(fits[[1]]$par))),
            start_large = c(fits[[2]]$par, utility = -fits[[2]]$value, scale = sum(abs(fits[[2]]$par)))), 4)
```

The two searches stop at coefficient vectors of very different scale with
almost the same utility and nearly the same direction: once the tilts are large
enough to drive most weights to zero, the truncated and renormalized weights
of @eq-18-longonly depend only on the ranking of $\boldsymbol{\theta}'\hat{\boldsymbol{x}}$
and are homogeneous of degree zero in $\boldsymbol{\theta}$, so the objective
flattens along a ray and the scale of the estimate is not identified. The
simplex restriction of the chapter avoids this by keeping the benchmark in
the policy.
